key_insight: High-damage He irradiation in single-crystal Al drives a transition from defect recombination to accumulation and sink-controlled absorption, culminating in Frank loop dissociation and stacking-fault tetrahedra formation that increases hardening.
engineering_relevance: The results help predict how aluminum reactor materials degrade under irradiation, informing alloy design and lifetime management for fission and other radiation environments.
method: Conventional cascade-overlap molecular dynamics for 50 keV He irradiation
Accelerated Iterative Kinetic Approach (IKA) to reach much higher accumulated damage
Benchmark comparison of IKA against cascade simulations
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that IKA reproduces the essential defect kinetics of cascade simulations while enabling access to substantially higher damage levels, revealing three degradation regimes.
watch_item: The study is focused on single-crystal Al at 300 K under 50 keV He irradiation, so transferability to alloys, polycrystals, and other temperatures or irradiation conditions may be limited.
paper_title: Mechanisms of Microstructural Evolution and Degradation in Aluminum under High-Damage Irradiation
